run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: Ran all three requested queries against the three app-280 log indices and, where the requested field was absent, re-ran against the field the index mappings actually carry. Index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' has no 'level' field (its fields are @timestamp, message, service, severity), so term level:ERROR returned 0 even over the full authorized window; the correct field term severity:ERROR returns 10 (severity buckets ERROR=10, INFO=6 across all 16 documents). Index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' has no 'level' and no 'severity' field; severity is numeric in 'severity_num' (integer), so terms level:["ERROR","FATAL"] returned 0, while severity_num buckets are 5->6, 3->5, 6->2 (13 documents) and document messages show [INFO] mapped to 3, [ERROR] to 5, [FATAL] to 6; terms severity_num:[5,6] therefore returns 8 = 6 ERROR + 2 FATAL. Index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' maps no date field at all (only ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message), so an @timestamp range query returned 0 with no time filter applied; the timestamp field is instead the keyword 'ingest_ts' (values like 2026-11-23T08:01:00). A keyword range on ingest_ts for 2026-11-23 combined with level:ERROR returns 7, and the same query for 2026-11-22 returns 5, against 12 total ERROR documents. Caveats: index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' holds no documents inside the default last-hour window (its data sits at 2026-11-03T20:13-20:14), so a default-window query on that index returns zero for any level; and index c has no date mapping, so its documents cannot be time-scoped by Elasticsearch itself.

claims.text: Index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' maps @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); there is no 'level' field in its mapping.

Query 1 as asked: {"term":{"level":"ERROR"}} on 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' returned total 0 (value 0, relation eq), both in the default last-hour window (2026-11-23T15:16:48Z-16:16:48Z) and over the full authorized window 2026-10-24T16:16:48Z-2026-11-23T16:16:48Z.
On the correct field, {"term":{"severity":"ERROR"}} on 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' over 2026-10-24T16:16:48Z-2026-11-23T16:16:48Z returned total 10.

A match-all query on 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' over the full authorized window matched 16 documents with severity buckets ERROR=10 and INFO=6, and sampled documents are service 'checkout-280' lines such as 'Health check 6' timestamped 2026-11-03T20:14:06Z.
Index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has no 'level' and no 'severity' field.
Query 2 as asked: {"terms":{"level":["ERROR","FATAL"]}} on 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' returned total 0.
Terms aggregation on 'severity_num' in 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' returned buckets key 5 = 6 docs, key 3 = 5 docs, key 6 = 2 docs (13 documents total) inside 2026-11-23T15:16:48Z-16:16:48Z.

The 13 documents of 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' show the numeric severity mapping in the msg text: '[INFO] healthcheck N' carries severity_num 3, '[ERROR] DB timeout N' carries severity_num 5, and '[FATAL] Disk full N' carries severity_num 6 (svc 'order-280', 2026-11-23T16:13:01Z-16:15:05Z).
On the correct field, {"terms":{"severity_num":[5,6]}} on 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' returned total 8 (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL) in 2026-11-23T15:16:48Z-16:16:48Z.
Index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' maps only ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it maps no date field, so no @timestamp field exists in that index.

Query 3 as asked: a range on '@timestamp' (2026-11-23T00:00:00Z to 2026-11-24T00:00:00Z) combined with term level:ERROR on 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' returned total 0, and the response notes that no matched index maps a date field so no time filter was applied.

With the index's actual timestamp field, term level:ERROR plus a keyword range on ingest_ts for 2026-11-23 (gte 2026-11-23T00:00:00, lt 2026-11-24T00:00:00) on 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' returned total 7.

The same ingest_ts keyword range applied to 2026-11-22 with term level:ERROR on 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' returned total 5, and level buckets for the whole index are ERROR=12 and INFO=4 across 16 documents with ingest_ts values only in 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-23 hours.
Document counts at query time are 16 for 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', 13 for 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3' and 16 for 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', all green/open.

'severity_num' in index b is a non-standard numeric encoding in which larger numbers do not mean less severe (INFO=3, ERROR=5, FATAL=6); the mapping is inferred from the sampled msg prefixes rather than from any documented scheme, so ERROR/FATAL must be selected as severity_num in (5,6) rather than by an inequality.

Query each index by the field its mapping actually carries: severity for index a, severity_num (numeric terms) for index b, and ingest_ts for index c; and always state an explicit start_time/end_time, because index a has no documents in the default last-hour window and index c has no date field, so a default-window query on either returns misleading zeros.

gaps: One view reported incomplete true (3f9f8125-812e-47fc-bca7-caf8a52e9bcb-t0:56add0cf-5f2f-4e31-a930-87b3f1e8672e): the match-all query on 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' matched 16 documents but only 4 were shown, so the document samples (all 'checkout-280' INFO health checks at 2026-11-03T20:13-20:14Z) are a partial sample; the severity bucket counts in that same view cover all 16 documents.

'Today's date' in question 3 is not defined by the request; the counts reported are for 2026-11-23 (the observation date, run at 2026-11-23T16:17Z) = 7 ERROR and 2026-11-22 = 5 ERROR. If a different 'today' was meant, that day's count was not measured.

Index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' maps no date field, so Elasticsearch cannot time-scope its documents; ingest_ts is a keyword and its values carry no timezone, so the day boundary used (2026-11-23T00:00:00 to 2026-11-24T00:00:00) is a lexicographic assumption, not a verified event time.

The numeric severity encoding in 'severity_num' (index b) is inferred from 13 sampled msg prefixes only; no mapping documentation or dictionary was available, so the treatment of unobserved values (e.g. 0,1,2,4,7) as ERROR/FATAL is unknown.
Index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3' has no documents in the default last-hour window (data at 2026-11-03T20:13-20:14), so its all-window counts are not representative of current activity.
next_steps: Confirm with the log producers/index templates whether 'severity_num' follows a known scheme, so ERROR/FATAL selection is not based on sampled correlation alone.
Consider mapping 'ingest_ts' as a date field in index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3' if time-range queries are expected on it.
